first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, making simplification the most direct path to recover durable qualified revenue. I would verify the prior onboarding result and compare it against the competitor-response evidence for promotional pricing before committing, while guarding against attracting low-retention or low-value accounts through discounts.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, the action most directly aligned with the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline. The verified source showed a durable improvement in completion and time-to-value, plus a 3% lift in 30-day retention, supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Monitor activation quality, qualified revenue, and retention rather than optimizing completion alone. Do not use promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue initially, the 12% retention decline indicates poor first-renewal survival and undermines long-term growth.

final2.rationale: Continue the onboarding simplification experiment rather than switching to broad promotional pricing. The verified onboarding result improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing the current activation and completion declines. The verified discount result showed a 12% retention decline despite short-term qualified-revenue lift, so deeper competitor pricing does not justify sacrificing sustainable revenue. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and qualified revenue by segment, and revisit targeted retention actions when verification capacity returns.
